items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The context is the mortal world among the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be given after proper testing?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is a fit recipient.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The chapter is numbered fifth
The unit is called a paṭala
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter of the Candradvīpa text.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the speaker come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
What is known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The speaker claims to have understood the Kaula doctrine through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared in the teaching
One question asks who that soul is
Another question asks what the soul's nature is
items.inference: The speaker seeks clarification of both the identity and essence of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul is asked about its place of dissolution
The speaker requests a complete account
The request is directed to the teacher
items.inference: The speaker asks for a full explanation of the soul's dissolution.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described here?
premises: The subject is described as supreme
It is described as partless and eternal
It is described as free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme individual soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is called supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is characterized as śakti and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual empowered by śakti.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath
It is described as situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The vital breath-air is present within all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul said to become immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated supreme Śiva
The statement is presented as a teaching
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through successive tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: The teaching is an esoteric oral transmission received through lineage.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is claimed to be effective through merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The teaching refers to this knowledge alone
The knowledge is received by hearing
The goddess is addressed directly
items.inference: Mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as having efficacy.
uncertainties: The sentence is syntactically incomplete and continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: The practice is to be undertaken for six months
The practitioner engages in the prescribed discipline
The result is described as free from bondage
items.inference: Six months of this practice yields a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact referent of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices this for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What two benefits result from the prescribed practice for the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
These outcomes follow the prior practice
items.inference: The practice brings freedom from disease and companionship with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
The subject communicated is the practice concerning the soul
The communication is declared complete
items.inference: The teaching on the practice of the soul has been conveyed to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What kind of recipient is qualified to receive this teaching according to inner resolve?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: The teaching should be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
uncertainties: The case forms of the two qualifiers differ in the transmitted text.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: To whom must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is linked to the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching of yoginī origin must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after the removal of ignorance?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body is now called pure
Previously it was struck by the veil of ignorance
items.inference: The speaker claims her body has become pure, freed from ignorance's veil.
uncertainties: The form deham appears where a nominative would be expected.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, no longer struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present desire
The desired topic is the overcoming of time
This knowledge is described as auspicious
items.inference: The speaker asks to hear the auspicious method for overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed by this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
The result stated is the destruction of death
items.inference: The teaching confidently claims a method by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the source of nectar?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar
There is contact with the essence of juice
Even a wise person is described as burning
items.inference: Even the wise may experience a burning sensation at the nectar's source.
uncertainties: The imagery of burning at the nectar-tip is obscure.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, at the tip of nectar, is burned by the essence of that juice.

items.question: What specific yogic action at the tongue and palate is prescribed for practice?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner acts upon the breath-air
The action is to drink the air slowly
items.inference: The practice involves slowly drawing in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath discipline continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is maintained for one year
The condition is sustained practice
The stated result is destruction of old age and death
items.inference: One year of this practice destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one accomplished in this practice?
premises: The person may be bitten by great serpents
Poison is the potential threat
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner is immune to serpent venom.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
